title: Chess Tournament Opening Prep Hit Rate
dataSources: BoardGameGeek plays (`bgg:play`), Poker Now sessions (`pokernow:session`), Bridge Base Online boards (`bridgebase:board`), and Lichess tournament rounds (`lichess:tournament`).
app: BoardGameGeek play logs, Poker Now session exports, Bridge Base Online boards, and Lichess tournament data ingested into Splunk.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=lichess:tournament opening_name=* prep_hit=*
| eval prep_hit=if(prep_hit="yes",1,0)
| stats sum(prep_hit) as prep_hits, count as games by opening_name
| eval prep_hit_pct=round(100*prep_hits/games,1)
| sort - prep_hit_pct
description: Shows how often your actual tournament games land in openings you prepared for ahead of time.
value: Prep is valuable only when it meets reality, and this hit-rate view tells you whether your study choices are aligned.
implementation: Stamp each Lichess round with whether the opening matched recent prep and summarize the percentage by opening name.
visualization: Bar chart of preparation hit rate by opening.
grandmaExplanation: It spots how often your chess preparation actually showed up on the board instead of something totally different.
